newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali police arrest Kashmiri, recover explosives.
newsitem.headline: Nepali police arrest Kashmiri, recover explosives.

text.p: Nepali police said on Tuesday they had arrested a suspected Kashmiri militant and seized 20 kg (44 lb) of explosives.
A police spokesman told Reuters that the plastic explosive RDX was recovered on Monday from a room rented by a Kashmiri carpet merchant in Nepal's capital, Kathmandu.
"He is a Kashmiri and is working for a terrorist group," senior police officer Dhurba Bahadur Pradhan told Reuters. He did not give any other details.
Dozens of separatist groups are fighting for Kashmir's independence or merger with Pakistan. Indian authorities claim some Kashmiri insurgents use Nepal as a base.

Police and hospital officials say more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence since the separatist revolt broke out in 1990 in India's Jammu and Kashmir state, which like Nepal lies in the Himalayan mountains.
The Kathmandu Post newspaper said Nepali authorities suspected militants might have intended to use the seized explosives in an attack in Delhi during India's Republic Day on January 26.
It said six detonators were also recovered.
